title: The Productivity Paradox
main_point: Spending three hours organizing a to-do list to avoid doing the actual tasks.
supporting_copy: Does the color-coding count as progress?
design_prompt: A 4:5 editorial graphic using a minimalist, high-contrast palette of cream, charcoal, and one accent color (electric blue). The composition features a split-screen visual metaphor. On the left side, a large, meticulously detailed checklist with various colored markers and checkboxes, labeled "To-Do List." On the right side, a single, small, untouched piece of paper labeled "Actual Work." The hierarchy places the Main_point as a bold header at the top center. The Supporting_copy is placed in a smaller, italicized font at the bottom center. Clean vector lines, ample negative space, and a modern sans-serif aesthetic.
caption: The most productive part of my day is planning how to be productive.
